title: Last Phase of Struggle for Independence

facts.text: The Act of 1935 provided for British governed provinces and Princely States to form a federation; the princely states refused to join as they would lose their autonomy, so the federal state was not brought into practice.
facts.quote: Act of 1935 : This Act made a provision for the British governed Indian provinces and Princely States to form a federation. ... If the princely states join the federation then they would lose their autonomy, hence they refused to join. Therefore the proposal of federal state in the Act was not brought into practice.

facts.text: In 1937 elections were held in eleven provinces; the Indian National Congress gained majority in eight provinces, and mixed cabinets were formed in the other three.
facts.quote: In 1937, elections were held in eleven provinces in the country. Among these, Indian National Congress gained majority over eight provinces and came to power. In other three provinces none of the party could achieve majority and therefore mixed cabinet was formed.

facts.text: Congress cabinet ministers released political prisoners, introduced basic education, prohibited liquor, improved the condition of the Dalits and passed an Act giving debt relief to farmers.
facts.quote: The Cabinet ministers of Indian National Congress did useful work for the people such as release of political prisoners from jail, introduction of basic education, prohibition of liquor, measures undertaken to improve condition of the Dalits, passing of Act giving debt relief to the farmers etc.

facts.text: The Second World War began in Europe in 1939, and Viceroy Lord Linlithgo declared that India had joined the war on the side of the British.
facts.quote: The Second World War began in Europe in 1939. The then Viceroy Lord Linlithgo declared that India has joined the war on the side of the British.

facts.text: England claimed to fight to save Democracy but refused to grant freedom to India, so the Congress provincial ministers resigned in November 1939.
facts.quote: England claimed that it is fighting to save Democracy in Europe. The Indian National Congress demanded that if the claim was true then England should immediately grant freedom to India. England refused to fulfill this demand and therefore the provincial ministers of Indian National Congress resigned in November 1939.

facts.text: Let us know: in the Individual Satyagraha every single person disobeyed the laws instead of a collective movement; Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi, followed by nearly 25,000 satyagrahis.
facts.quote: it was decided that instead of a collective movement, every single person should disobey the laws. This was known as 'Individual Satyagraha'. Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi of individual satyagraha. He was followed by nearly 25,000 satyagrahis who accepted imprisonment for their participation.

facts.text: As the Japanese army reached India's eastern borders, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill sent Sir Stafford Cripps, who put up a proposal in March 1942.
facts.quote: The Japanese army reached the eastern borders of India. ... Hence the British Prime Minister Winston Churchill sent Sir Stafford Cripps to India. In March 1942, he put up a proposal of India in front of the Indians.

facts.text: The Congress rejected the Cripps proposal as there was no clear mention of complete independence; the Muslim League rejected it as there was no mention of creation of Pakistan.
facts.quote: The Indian National Congress rejected the proposal since there was no clear mention of complete independence. Since there was no mention of creation of Pakistan, the Muslim League also rejected the Cripps Mission.

facts.text: On 14 July 1942 the Congress Working Committee passed a resolution at Wardha demanding that British rule in India end immediately.
facts.quote: The Working Committee of the Congress passed a resolution on 14 July 1942 at Wardha. The resolution demanded that the British rule in India be ended immediately and India should be given independence.

facts.text: On 7 August 1942 the Congress session was held at Gowalia Tank (Kranti Maidan) in Mumbai, with Maulana Abul Kalam Azad as President.
facts.quote: On 7 August 1942, the session of Indian National Congress was held at Gowalia Tank (Kranti Maidan) in Mumbai. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the President of this session.

facts.text: On 8 August 1942 the 'Quit India' resolution put forth by Jawaharlal Nehru was passed with great majority, and a nation wide non violent agitation under Mahatma Gandhi was decided.
facts.quote: On 8 August the resolution of 'Quit India' put forth by Jawaharlal Nehru got passed with great majority. It was also decided to start a nation wide non violent agitation under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.

facts.text: Gandhiji said 'we shall either free India or die in the attempt' and appealed to the public to sacrifice with the feeling of 'Do or Die'.
facts.quote: we shall either free India or die in the attempt." Gandhiji made an inspirational appeal to the public to be ready to sacrifice with the feeling of 'Do or Die'.

facts.text: After the leaders' arrest, agitators attacked jails, police stations and railway stations; in Maharashtra people struggled at places like Chimur, Ashti, Yavali, Mahad and Gargoti.
facts.quote: The agitators attacked some places jails, police stations, railway stations etc. ... In Maharashtra, the young and old struggled with determination and boundless courage at places like Chimur, Ashti, Yavali, Mahad, Gargoti etc.

facts.text: Do you know: at Nandurbar, school children led by Shirishkumar marched with the tri colour flag and gave the slogan 'Vande Mataram'; in the police firing Shirishkumar, Laldas, Dhansukhlal, Shashidhar and Ghanashyam became martyrs.
facts.quote: At Nandurbar, the school children, under the leadership of Shirishkumar, carried out procession holding the tri colour flag. The slogan of 'Vande Mataram' was given. ... In this firing Shirishkumar, Laldas, Dhansukhlal, Shashidhar, Ghanashyam, these school children became martyr.

facts.text: At the end of 1942 the leadership of the movement went to young socialist activists such as Jayprakash Narayan, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali, Yashwantrao Chavan and Usha Mehta.
facts.quote: At the end of 1942 the public movement got a new turn. The leadership of this movement went into hands of young socialist activists. Jayprakash Narayan, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, ... Aruna Asaf Ali, ... Yashwantrao Chavan, Vasantdada Patil, Maganlal Bagdi, Usha Mehta such leaders were in the forefront.

facts.text: Underground activists disrupted transport and communication by breaking railway routes, cutting telephone lines and blowing up bridges.
facts.quote: The activist disrupted the transport and communication as well as the government machinery by causing the breakdown of Railway routes, cutting of telephone line, blowing up bridges etc.

facts.text: Hemu Kalani in Sindh province tried to destroy the railway carrying British troops and supplies and was hanged to death.
facts.quote: Hemu Kalani, in Sindh province, tried to destroy the railway along with his companions when he received the news of passing of a railway carrying British troops and supplies. The court punished him to be hanged to death.

facts.text: Bhai Kotwal's 'Azad Dasta' in Karjat taluka (Raigad district) and General Awari's 'Lal Sena' in Nagpur made the government helpless for months.
facts.quote: Bhai Kotwal's 'Azad Dasta' in Karjat taluka of modern day Raigad district, General Awari's 'Lal Sena' in Nagpur such groups made the government helpless and witless for months.

facts.text: In Mumbai, Vitthal Zaveri, Usha Mehta and companions set up the secret transmission centre 'Azad Radio'; such centres also operated at Kolkata, Delhi and Pune.
facts.quote: In Mumbai, Vitthal Zaveri, Usha Mehta and her companions established a secret transmission centre named 'Azad Radio'. ... Such transmission centres operated at Kolkata, Delhi and Pune for some period of time.

facts.text: Parallel Governments ('People's Government') were formed in Midnapore in Bengal, Ballia and Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh, and Purnia in Bihar.
facts.quote: At some places in the country, British officers were driven out and the 'People's Government' was established. These are called 'Parallel Government'. Parallel Government where formed in districts of Midnapore in Bengal, Ballia and Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh and Purnia in Bihar.

facts.text: In Satara district of Maharashtra, in 1942, Krantisinh Nana Patil ended British government and established a parallel government.
facts.quote: In Satara district of Maharashtra, in 1942, Krantisinh Nana Patil brought an end to the British government and established parallel government.

facts.text: At Kundal, 'Toofan Sena' was established under Krantiagrani G. D. alias Bapu Lad.
facts.quote: At Kundal, under the leadership of Krantiagrani G. D. alias Bapu Lad, 'Toofan Sena' was established.

facts.text: The Parallel Government collected taxes, kept law and order, punished criminals and ran People's Courts; its constructive work included opposing money lenders and caste distinctions, prohibiting liquor and spreading literacy.
facts.quote: collection of taxes, maintenance of law and order, punishment to criminals, such work was done by the Parallel Government. People started accepting the verdict passed by the People's Court ... Opposition to money lenders, prohibition on liquor, spread of literacy, opposition to caste distinctions many such constructive work was done by this government.

facts.text: So many joined the 1942 struggle that all the prisons were not enough; songs by Sane Guruji and Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj inspired agitators; the movement is also called 'August Kranti'.
facts.quote: The number of people participating in the struggle was so huge that even all the prisons in the whole of the country were not enough to contain them. The patriotic songs composed by Sane Guruji, Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj and others increased the enthusiasm of the agitators. This nationwide movement is also called 'August Kranti'.

facts.text: Subhash Chandra Bose was President of Congress twice; after differences with senior leaders he resigned and founded the 'Forward Bloc'.
facts.quote: He graced the position of President of Congress twice. ... As a result, Subhash Chandra Bose resigned from the position of President. To place his views in front of the people he founded a party known as 'Forward Bloc'.

facts.text: Interned in his residence, Bose escaped in disguise, reached Germany in April 1941, founded the 'Free India Centre' and spoke from the Berlin Radio station.
facts.quote: the British Government interned him in his residence. From there he escaped in disguise. In April 1941 he reached Germany. There he founded the 'Free India Centre'. From the Berlin Radio station in Germany, he appealed to the Indian people to join in an armed struggle.

facts.text: Rash Behari Bose had been staying in Japan since 1915 and established the 'Indian Independence League'; he invited Subhash Chandra Bose to Japan.
facts.quote: Rash Behari Bose invited Subhash Chandra Bose to Japan. ... Rash Behari Bose was staying in Japan since 1915. He had organised the Indian patriots living in countries of South East Asia and established the organisation named 'Indian Independence League'.

facts.text: After Japan's conquests in early 1942, Rash Behari Bose with Captain Mohan Singh formed a battalion of Indian Prisoners of War named the 'Indian National Army' (Azad Hind Sena), later led by Netaji.
facts.quote: Rash Behari Bose, with the help of Captain Mohan Singh, formed a battalion of these Indian Prisoners of War. It was named as 'Indian National Army' (Azad Hind Sena). Later Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army.

facts.text: In October 1943 Netaji established the Azad Hind Government in Singapore; his chief associates included Shah Nawaz Khan, Jagannath Bhosale, Dr.Laxmi Swaminathan, Gurubuksh Sing Dhillon and Prem Kumar Sehgal.
facts.quote: In October 1943, Netaji established Azad Hind Government in Singapore. Shah Nawaz Khan, Jagannath Bhosale, Dr.Laxmi Swaminathan, Gurubuksh Sing Dhillon, Prem Kumar Sehgal etc. were his chief associates.

facts.text: Captain Laxmi Swaminathan was the Commander of the Rani of Jhansi Regiment.
facts.quote: Captain Laxmi Swaminathan was the Commander of Rani of Jhansi Regiment.

facts.text: Netaji appealed: 'You give me blood and I will give you independence'.
facts.quote: Netaji appealed to the Indian people- 'You give me blood and I will give you independence'.

facts.text: In November 1943 Japan conquered the Andaman and Nicobar islands and handed them to the Azad Hind Government; Netaji renamed them 'Shahid' and 'Swarajya' respectively.
facts.quote: In November 1943, Japan conquered Andaman and Nicobar islands and handed them over to Azad Hind Government. Netaji renamed them as 'Shahid' and 'Swarajya' respectively.

facts.text: In 1944 the Indian National Army captured the Aarakan province in Myanmar and posts on the eastern border of Assam; the Imphal campaign remained incomplete because Japan stopped helping.
facts.quote: In 1944, Indian National Army captured the Aarakan province in Myanmar. Posts on the eastern border of Assam were captured. In the same period the campaign of Imphal remained incomplete because Japan stopped helping the Indian National Army.

facts.text: Japan accepted defeat; on 18 August 1945 Subhash Chandra Bose died in a plane accident, and the soldiers of the Indian National Army laid down their arms.
facts.quote: Japan accepted defeat. On 18 August 1945 Subhash Chandra Bose died in a plane accident. On this background the soldiers of Indian National Army had to lay down their arms.

facts.text: INA officers charged with treason were defended by Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai and Tej Bahadur Sapre; the military tribunal gave life imprisonment, but unrest forced the British to suspend the punishments.
facts.quote: the British Government charged the officers of Indian National Army with treason. Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapre these expert lawyers defended them. But the military tribunal held the officers guilty and they were sentenced to life imprisonment. ... Finally the British Government had to suspend the punishments given by the military tribunal.

facts.text: The naval revolt burst out on the British war ship 'Talwar' in Mumbai on 18 February 1946; the soldiers unfurled the tri colour flag on it.
facts.quote: It burst out on the British war ship 'Talwar' in Mumbai on 18 February 1946. The soldiers unfurled the tri colour flag on the British warship.

facts.text: With the mediation of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the naval soldiers laid down their arms.
facts.quote: Finally with the mediation of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the naval soldiers laid down their arms.

facts.text: To support the naval soldiers, Air force officers from Delhi, Lahore, Karachi, Ambala, Meerut etc. went on strike.
facts.quote: To support the uprising of naval soldiers, the Air force officers from Delhi, Lahore, Karachi, Ambala, Meerut etc. went on strike.

facts.text: The period between 1942 and 1946 shook the foundation of British power in India; Army, Navy and Air Force, the backbone of British power, were now opposing the British.
facts.quote: In this way the period between 1942 to 1946 shook the foundation of British power in India. ... Army, Navy and Air Force was the backbone of British power. They were also now opposing the British.
